messages:
alex: FYI ran AWQ-int4-hybrid on new-70b-open for onboarding and I'm seeing a weird CSV/date swap + repeated header rows in generated CSVs. Small sample below.

alex: ```prompt: export_csv(table) -> header
output: "id,name,date
id,name,date
1,Acme,03/01/2025
2,Globex,03/02/2025
"
expected: "id,name,date
1,Acme,01/03/2025
2,Globex,02/03/2025
``` 

maya: Is this limited to CSV/table extraction workloads or do other tasks show it too?

alex: Mostly CSV and SQL->CSV routes, also noticed in a few code-gen prompts where date literals are swapped. Quick numbers: CSV correctness dropped from ~98% (FP8 baseline) to ~62% under AWQ-int4-hybrid. Code pass@1 went 84% -> 73%.

li: Can you paste the exact quant command/profile you used?

alex: ```bash
redwood quant run --model new-70b-open --recipe awq-int4-hybrid --pack-size 16 --seed 42 --profile hybrid_v2.json
```

jordaan: Did you try disabling KV cache or changing pack_size? AWQ's packing and kv-layout differ from GPTQ so token alignment bugs can show up.

alex: Reran with --disable-kv-cache: issue reduces but not gone (CSV swap rate ~3% -> 1.1%). Canary logs show spike on /export/csv route.

ci-bot: canary deploy new-70b-open-awq-int4 to shared-pool-3: requests=120, error_rate=3.9%, avg_latency=210ms, anomalies=[csv_field_swap: 3.9%]

maya: My hunch is tokenization boundary around separators like '-' and '/'. If AWQ packing shifts prompt token offsets, date substrings can map to different token sequences. Try forcing byte-level tokenization or pack_size=1 to see if it disappears.

li: Also check if model has special DATE/NUMBER tokens in the vocabulary. Run targeted eval on 'date-csv' set and diff token IDs before/after quant.

alex: Quick eval diff snippet:
```
orig tokens: [482, 12, 99, 1001, 300] -> decode: '\"01/03/2025\"'
awq tokens:  [482, 12, 99, 1002, 300] -> decode: '\"03/01/2025\"'
// Observe token index +1 at position 4 after comma, looks like packing misalignment
```

jordaan: Possible fixes: enforce block-aligned packing, or add KV alignment padding. I'll run an experiment: awq-int4-hybrid + pack_size=1 + pack_align=true and compare diffs.

maya: If that fixes it we should add a canary check to compare field ordering/values on CSV exports and block rollouts unless csv_field_swap_rate < 0.1%. Also add a targeted unit test in the eval harness for date formats.

li: Follow-ups: jordaan -> run pack_align experiment and post results. alex -> create repro script with exact seed/dataset and attach. maya -> add canary metric 'csv_field_swap_rate' to per-route checks.

alex: Creating repro now, will upload script & minimal dataset to the eng-ml bucket and post link.

jordaan: Experiment started (pack_align=true, pack_size=1). ETA ~2h. Will post diff and per-task metrics when done.

alex: Thanks — ping me when you have the run. :thumbsup:
